newsitem.title: UK: Boeing sees trade war if merger blocked - FT.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sees trade war if merger blocked - FT.

text.p: Boeing Co warned the European Commission it risked provoking a transatlantic trade war if it tried to block the U.S. group's proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp, the Financial Times said on Wednesday.

The newspaper said the Seattle-based aircraft maker was responding to European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert's statement on Tuesday that he would not accept the proposed merger as it currently stood.

The Commission has the power to vet mergers or acquisitions involving companies that make over 250 million ECUs in sales in the European Union and have a combined global turnover of five billion ECUs.
The newspaper said Boeing was concerned the Commission might impose a fine on the merged group of 10 percent of its revenues.
The two companies, whose merger would create the world's biggest aerospace and defence group, expect to have combined revenues of 48 billion dollars.
Boeing said it had responded to Van Miert's requests for further information but it reserved its right to challenge the Commission's jurisdiction over the proposed merger.
The Commission is expected to set out its objections to the proposed merger over the next 10 days.
But Boeing said Van Miert's statements suggested he might have prejudged the issue, the Financial Times said.
